brief: JPMorgan Prime Finance reports equities stayed resilient in September but rotated beneath the surface: AI/Tech stocks kept supporting the broader market even as rate-sensitive areas and some cyclicals were sold. The rotation benefited Quant hedge funds (up 2-2.5% MTD) while Equity L/S lagged (-1.5% MTD, overall HF performance -0.7% MTD, +8.1% YTD), because longs performed poorly in aggregate. Short-side alpha bounced back, with crowding improving across regions except US Health Care, still the top North American crowding detractor (Biotech posted its sharpest 60-day de-grossing since early 2020). Tech crowding rebounded: funds bought Mag7 (+3z over 20 days, mostly longs) and US Semis, while EU Semis were sold and Asia AI/Tech flows were mixed. US gross flows reached a seasonal high, rebounding from the July-August de-gross in a pattern resembling 2022 and driven by Quants, though shorts could stay elevated into mid-October if yields keep pressuring risk. Regionally, US positioning held roughly neutral while Europe and China/AxJ saw the biggest reductions, with Europe's slide triggering a tactical buy signal.
